description: Curated MITRE ATT&CK v14 subset — top 50 techniques, 14 tactics, 20 APT groups. Bundled for offline/air-gapped deployments.

objects.name: Reconnaissance
objects.description: Gathering information to plan future adversary operations.

objects.name: Resource Development
objects.description: Establishing resources to support operations.

objects.name: Initial Access
objects.description: Techniques to gain initial foothold in a network.

objects.name: Execution
objects.description: Techniques that result in adversary-controlled code running.

objects.name: Persistence
objects.description: Techniques to maintain foothold across restarts.

objects.name: Privilege Escalation
objects.description: Gaining higher-level permissions.

objects.name: Defense Evasion
objects.description: Avoiding detection and defenses.

objects.name: Credential Access
objects.description: Stealing account credentials.

objects.name: Discovery
objects.description: Figuring out the environment.

objects.name: Lateral Movement
objects.description: Moving through the environment.

objects.name: Collection
objects.description: Gathering data of interest.

objects.name: Command and Control
objects.description: Communicating with compromised systems.

objects.name: Exfiltration
objects.description: Stealing data from the network.

objects.name: Impact
objects.description: Manipulating, interrupting, or destroying systems.

objects.name: PowerShell
objects.description: Adversaries may abuse PowerShell commands and scripts for execution.

objects.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
objects.description: Adversaries may abuse command and script interpreters to execute commands, scripts, or binaries.

objects.name: Phishing
objects.description: Adversaries may send phishing messages to gain access to victim systems.

objects.name: OS Credential Dumping
objects.description: Adversaries may attempt to dump credentials to obtain account login information.

objects.name: Remote Services
objects.description: Adversaries may use Valid Accounts to log into a service specifically designed to accept remote connections.

objects.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
objects.description: Adversaries may steal data by exfiltrating it over an existing command and control channel.

objects.name: Masquerading
objects.description: Adversaries may attempt to manipulate features of artifacts to make them appear legitimate.

objects.name: Spearphishing Attachment
objects.description: Adversaries may send spearphishing emails with a malicious attachment.

objects.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
objects.description: Adversaries may transfer tools or other files from an external system into a compromised environment.

objects.name: Application Layer Protocol
objects.description: Adversaries may communicate using OSI application layer protocols.

objects.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
objects.description: Adversaries may encrypt data on target systems or on large numbers of systems in a network to interrupt availability.

objects.name: Valid Accounts
objects.description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts.

objects.name: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
objects.description: Adversaries may achieve persistence by adding a program to a commonly used registry run key.

objects.name: Process Injection
objects.description: Adversaries may inject code into processes to evade process-based defenses.

objects.name: System Network Configuration Discovery
objects.description: Adversaries may look for details about the network configuration and settings.

objects.name: Brute Force
objects.description: Adversaries may use brute force techniques to gain access to accounts.

objects.name: SQL Injection
objects.description: Adversaries may attempt to take advantage of a weakness in an Internet-facing computer.

objects.name: APT28
objects.description: A Russian GRU-associated threat actor targeting government and military organizations.

objects.name: APT29
objects.description: Russian SVR threat actor known for SolarWinds supply chain attack.

objects.name: APT41
objects.description: Chinese state-sponsored threat actor conducting espionage and financially motivated attacks.

objects.name: Lazarus Group
objects.description: North Korean state-sponsored group behind WannaCry and financial heists.

objects.name: FIN7
objects.description: Financially motivated threat actor targeting hospitality and financial sectors.

objects.name: Sandworm
objects.description: Russian GRU unit responsible for NotPetya and Ukrainian power grid attacks.

objects.name: Turla
objects.description: Long-running FSB-affiliated espionage actor with custom rootkits.

objects.name: Equation Group
objects.description: Highly sophisticated NSA-linked threat actor behind Stuxnet precursor tools.

objects.name: OilRig
objects.description: Iranian MOIS threat actor targeting Middle East and Africa.

objects.name: Kimsuky
objects.description: North Korean cyber espionage group targeting South Korea and US.
